steps: Install FuelSteps from the Connect IQ app on your phone; after the sync the watch asks to install it, pick the running activity › OK.
Allow the alert on the watch: activity settings › Alerts › Add New › Connect IQ › FuelSteps › On (the watch may ask this during installation).

Edit your schedules in the Connect IQ app: My data fields › FuelSteps › Settings › Save. Schedule 1 "Gel 5 km" is ready to go (3× 5 km, 25 g gel with caffeine). Build your own schedule and copy the fields.
Pick a schedule on the watch before the run: hold UP › Connect IQ fields › FuelSteps. Nothing fires until you do, and after the run it is off again, like a navigation route.

Summary: total carbs, fuel moments, caffeine moments and schedule

faq: FuelSteps is a free data field for Garmin watches (Connect IQ) that reminds you when to take a gel or other fuel during a run. You build your own schedule by distance or time, and FuelSteps vibrates, beeps and shows a full-screen alert just before each moment.
Which Garmin watches does FuelSteps support?

All round Garmin watches with Connect IQ 5.0 or newer, including Forerunner 165, 170, 255, 265, 570, 70, 955, 965 and 970, fēnix 7, 8, 9 and E, epix (Gen 2) and epix Pro, Enduro 3, MARQ (Gen 2), Venu 2, 3 and 4, and vívoactive 5 and 6.
Can I mix different fuels in one schedule?
Yes. Every step has its own name (for example Gel, Dextro or Gel CAF), its own grams of carbohydrate and an optional caffeine mark. Steps can repeat, and repeats are numbered automatically.
Can I plan by distance or by time?
Both. Each schedule is either all distance (km) or all time (minutes), with steps from 0.5 to 100 km or from 5 to 600 minutes.
Why does the alert come early?

By default the alert comes 60 seconds or 150 metres before the planned moment, so it doesn't clash with Garmin's own km or lap alert. You can set it from 0 (exactly on the moment) up to 3 minutes or 300 metres.
Why do my alerts come a little before the aid stations in a race?

Your watch measures a little more distance than the official course: you never run the ideal line, and GPS wobbles. On a distance schedule set to the official aid-station kilometres, the alerts therefore come slightly earlier as the race goes on. That works in your favour: the reminder arrives before you reach the table.
Do I have to press a button when I take a gel?

No. FuelSteps is a reminder, not a log. It saves the planned carbs in your activity, shown as charts in Garmin Connect, without button presses that could disturb your recording. The charts and totals are marked "planned": they show what the schedule said, so if you skip a gel the chart won't know.
Yes. FuelSteps is free, with no subscription, no ads and no account. [Donations] are appreciated.

plan_format_lead: For people who prefer typing, and for AI assistants: this is exactly what FuelSteps expects in Garmin Connect.
plan_format_li: Garmin Connect (Connect IQ app › My data fields › FuelSteps › Settings) has 15 fields per schedule, 5 schedules in total: Import (max 256 characters, see below), Name (max 16 characters), Unit (Distance = km or Time = min) and Step 1 to Step 12 (text, max 40 characters). Unused fields must contain -; Garmin Connect cannot save an empty field. Dashed fields are skipped, so put a dash in every field you don't use.
One step field: [Nx] size [text] [carbsg] [caf] or @position [text] [carbsg] [caf], separated by spaces, in this order.
Nx: optional repeat, 1–30. 3x5 = three times 5 km or 5 min; the watch numbers them #1, #2, #3.
size: distance or time after the previous moment (km with Distance, minutes with Time), decimals with . or ,. Minimum 0.5 km or 5 min; a schedule may add up to 100 km or 600 min.

@position: instead of a size, the position from the start: @21 = at km 21 (or minute 21). Handy for aid stations at fixed kilometres; mixes with relative steps, must lie at least 0.5 km or 5 min after the previous moment, no repeat.
text: optional, may contain spaces and numbers (Gel CAF, Gel 100), default Gel. Only a last word like 25g is read as grams, so a product name with a number stays text.
carbs: optional, whole grams, always with a g: 25g, default 0.
caf: optional, any case, marks caffeine (shown on the alert, counted in the activity).
0 as size is only allowed in Step 1 without repeat: the gel you take before the start, counted in the totals, no alert.

Import: the whole schedule in one field, name;km|min;step;step;…, separated by ;, on one line or one item per line as on this page, e.g. Long run;km;0 Gel 25g;10 Gel 25g;3x5 Gel 25g. While Import holds anything but -, the Name, Unit and Step fields of that schedule are ignored and an error names the step's position in the import text. Keep it under 256 characters; Garmin Connect may cut longer text off.
One invalid field makes the whole schedule invalid; the menu on the watch names the field.

plan_format_worked_b: Field by field that is Name Long run, Unit Distance, Step 1 0 Gel 25g, Step 2 10 Gel 25g, Step 3 5 Dextro 15g, Step 4 2x5 Gel 25g, Step 5 5 Gel CAF 25g caf, Step 6 to 12 -. Moments: gel before the start, km 10 gel, km 15 Dextro, km 20 and 25 gel (#1, #2), km 30 caffeine gel. Total 140 g, 6 moments, 1 with caffeine. The alert comes 150 m before each moment by default.
plan_note_p: FuelSteps was built to let you click your steps together right inside the Connect IQ app, and that version was nearly finished. Garmin Connect currently cannot save list-type settings for Connect IQ apps (a known issue Garmin has acknowledged), so the step fields are plain text for now. This builder fills that gap. Once Garmin resolves it, building schedules can move into the app.
